title: Family of teen killed by police taking City of Winnipeg, WPS and its chief to court
article: The family of Eishia Hudson on Wednesday filed a lawsuit against the City of Winnipeg, police Chief Danny Smyth, and two unnamed police officers 20 months after the shooting death of the 16-year-old Indigenous girl.

Hudson was shot on April 8, 2020, after a stolen vehicle with several occupants was chased by members of the Winnipeg Police Service following a liquor store robbery. According to a press release from Cochrane Saxberg Barristers & Solicitors, the law firm representing the family, Smyth is being sued for his alleged failure to adequately address systemic racism towards Indigenous people in the Winnipeg Police Service. The two officers are accused of "acts of recklessness, carelessness, and negligence that resulted in the death of Eishia."

"Eishia's death brought us closer to families across the country who suffered the same loss of loved ones at the hands of police misuse of force," said William Hudson, father of Eishia, in the press release. "We are all on the search for justice. The police must be held accountable. If Eishia wasn't recognized as being Indigenous by the police officer, she might still be alive today."
Winnipeg police shot and killed Eishia Hudson, 16, on Wednesday, April 8, 2020. The shooting took place at Lagimodiere Boulevard and Fermor Avenue. Winnipeg Sun file

Cochrane Saxberg said there have been a disproportionate number of Indigenous people killed by Winnipeg police since 2000. The civil claim says the officer who shot Eishia identified her as an Indigenous teenage male prior to firing his gun, allegedly at close range.

Indigenous people in Canada are 10 times more likely to be shot and killed by police than Caucasians, says a 2020 CTV News report. Between 2017 and 2020, 25 Indigenous people were shot and killed by RCMP officers.
The Centers for Disease Control & Prevention in the U.S. says Indigenous people are killed by police officers more than any other demographic.

"The problem of police killing Indigenous people has only escalated since the release of the Aboriginal Justice Inquiry's Final Report," said Danielle Morrison, co-counsel for the family in the press release. "This claim cannot ignore the alarming numbers that threaten the lives of Indigenous people."
Cochrane Saxberg said of the 28 people killed by Manitoba police between 2000 and 2020, 17 were Indigenous, adding a third of the deaths happened in 2019 and 2020.

However, Manitoba's Independent Investigation Unit in 2020 released a final report into the matter, saying no criminal charges would be brought against the police officers. An Inquest into Eishia's death is pending.

"The family needs its day in court to hold the Winnipeg Police Service accountable for what appears to be a prima facie case of excessive force resulting in the tragic death of a 16-year-old Indigenous girl," said Kris Saxberg, co-counsel for the family in the press release. "The Inquest process does not have the scope to ascribe civil culpability. This lawsuit gives the family that opportunity."
Pivotal to the lawsuit is The Fatal Accidents Act, which allows families of deceased people to file a claim and recover damages if the fatality was due to a wrongful act or negligence.
The Winnipeg Police Service declined to comment on the matter.
